cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities arising from improper handling of user-supplied data during cookie parsing and output generation. Common issues include missing validation of control characters in Set-Cookie headers, unsafe deserialization of cookie data using pickle, prototype pollution from untrusted cookie names, over-broad whitespace trimming causing normalization bypass, and missing output encoding leading to XSS. These flaws allow attackers to inject arbitrary headers, execute arbitrary code, pollute object prototypes, bypass security prefixes, or perform cross-site scripting.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 4 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Add validation functions to reject or escape characters that can break the HTTP header syntax (e.g., control characters, \r\n, ;) before constructing the Set-Cookie header string..

sub_patterns.name: Missing validation of special characters in Set-Cookie header construction
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumes cookie names, values, domains, and paths are safe to embed directly into HTTP Set-Cookie headers without sanitization, allowing injection of control characters (CR, LF) or delimiter characters (semicolon) that can break the header format or inject arbitrary headers.
